topic.name: Calculating Limits of Rational Functions by Factoring

question.explanation:
If we attempt to evaluate the limit, we get an indeterminate form: \[ \eqalign{ \displaystyle{\lim_{x\to 0} \dfrac{9x^3-4x}{3x^2+2x}} & = \dfrac{9(0)^3-4(0)}{3(0)^2+2(0)} = \dfrac{0}{0} }\]

So, to find the limit, we have to factor the numerator and the denominator. We get \begin{align*} \dfrac{9x^3-4x}{3x^2+2x}&=\dfrac{x\left(9x^2-4\right)}{x\left(3x+2\right)}\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{9x^2-4}{3x+2}. \end{align*}

Therefore,

\begin{align*} \displaystyle{\lim_{x\to 0}} \dfrac{9x^3-4x}{3x^2+2x} &=\displaystyle{\lim_{x\to 0}} \dfrac{9x^2-4}{3x+2}\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{0-4}{0+2}\\[5pt] &=-2. \end{align*}

example.title: Calculating the Limit of a Rational Function With Higher Order Terms by Factoring

question.explanation:
If we attempt to evaluate the limit, we get an indeterminate form:

\[ \eqalign{ \lim_\limits{x \rightarrow -1} \dfrac{x^2-2x-3}{x^2-1} & = \dfrac{(-1)^2-2(-1)-3}{(-1)^2-1} = \dfrac{0}{0} }\]

So, to find the limit, we have to factor the numerator and the denominator. We get \[ \eqalign{ \dfrac{x^2-2x-3}{x^2-1} & = \dfrac{(x+1)(x-3)}{(x-1)(x+1)} \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{x-3}{x-1}. }\]

Therefore, \[ \eqalign{ \lim_{x \rightarrow -1} \dfrac{x^2-2x-3}{x^2-1} & = \lim_{x \rightarrow -1} \dfrac{x-3}{x-1} \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{-1-3}{-1-1} \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{-4}{-2}\\[5pt] &= 2. }\]

example.title: Calculating the Limit of a Rational Function With Two Quadratic Terms by Factoring

question.explanation:
If we attempt to evaluate the limit, we get an indeterminate form: \[ \eqalign{ \displaystyle{\lim_{y\to 3} \dfrac{y^3-9y}{y^2-5y+6}} & =\dfrac{3^3-9(3)}{3^2-5(3)+6}= \dfrac{0}{0} }\]

So, to find the limit, we have to factor the numerator and the denominator. We get \begin{align*} \dfrac{y^3-9y}{y^2-5y+6}&=\dfrac{y(y^2-9)}{(y-2)(y-3)}\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{y\left(y-3\right)(y+3)}{(y-2)(y-3)}\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{y(y+3)}{(y-2)} \end{align*}

Therefore, \begin{align*} \displaystyle{\lim_{y\to 3} \dfrac{y^3-9y}{y^2-5y+6}} &=\displaystyle{\lim_{y\to 3} \dfrac{y(y+3)}{y-2}}\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{3(3+3)}{3-2}\\[5pt] &=18. \end{align*}
